tagline: Pucks in a burning building hear the occupants' phones; each phone appears in the right room of a map built from the building's own data (record, aerial, 3D twin), drawn only as precisely as the measurement allows, and an AI command agent routes the rescue and writes the report.
abstract: When a commercial building is on fire, the incident commander's hardest question is who is still inside, and where. Sandtable Beacon is a command and reporting centre for that question. When the alarm comes in, an AI command agent reads three layers for the address (the building record with its tenants, the aerial image, the 3D twin) and writes the pre-incident plan. A crew then places small pucks (Qorvo DWM3001CDK boards: Bluetooth and UWB) in the building. Occupants who opened the opt-in app are ranged through their phones, and each phone is drawn as what the measurement supports: a ring, two candidate points, or one point, in the right room and beside the tenant the building record expects there. Phones without the app are only a device count. The agent prioritises, routes a rescue crew through the twin, issues the radio order, re-plans and writes the report the command post keeps. Sponsor layers run as labelled fixtures; positions are simulated until the boards run.
aha: Two pucks give each phone two possible places, mirror images of each other; the twin's walls rule one out, so phone 1 lands as a point in the dentist's office the building record expects to be full, while phone 2 honestly stays 'two places: search both'. The building's own data does the job of a third puck.
how_it_works: Pre-plan: a tool-using agent reads the building record (CoStar layer), the aerial image (Vexcel layer, through a vision tool) and the 3D twin (Matterport layer)
Pucks in: DWM3001CDK boards on stock firmware, positions tape-measured and clicked onto the plan; opt-in iPhones range them and report status (lane L16's Beacon module)
Drawn honestly: one puck a ring, two pucks two candidates, the twin deletes impossible ones, a point only for a fix; no app means a device count, never people
Accountability: the record's tenants and expected occupancy per suite set against the phones heard, as ranges
Command: the agent prioritises, routes a crew through the twin, radios the order, re-routes when a phone's geometry improves, requests EMS
Report and feeds: a printable command-post report, GeoJSON and Cursor-on-Target
stack: Claude via the Anthropic SDK, the Claude CLI, or replay of recorded real runs (claude-sonnet-5-5 recordings)
Lane L16 Beacon module (vendor/beacon): locator, tracker, simulator, iOS app (Apple Nearby Interaction)
Qorvo DWM3001CDK on stock Nearby Interaction firmware
Bench uwb-kit (vendor/uwbkit) for the simulated Crews mode
Scout radar simulator and DSP adapted from lane L08
Public open data: LA County assessor and LARIAC, City of LA business listings and GeoHub, US Census TIGERweb, USDA NAIP

sponsor_tech.costar: Building record: tenants by suite and floor, business category (life hazards inferred), vacancy, construction, stories, area; drives who-is-expected-where in the accountability table and the agent's priorities. Fixture mode only (real public data for 7325 Medical Center Dr, Los Angeles, CoStar-only fields empty); live adapter is a mapping table to fill (docs/TOOLKIT_SWAP.md).
sponsor_tech.matterport: 3D twin: rooms, walls, doors, stairs, walking graph; routes the crew and prunes impossible phone candidates (outside the outline, inside a wall, behind a wall on a line-of-sight link). Fixture: synthetic interior fitted to the real footprint. Live adapter written against the Model API GraphQL samples, never called.
sponsor_tech.vexcel: Aerial: the sides of the building, approach, staging, hydrants; the agent looks at the image through a vision tool. Fixture: real USDA NAIP imagery. Live adapter written from the public Vexcel API v2 OpenAPI spec, never called.
sponsor_tech.anthropic: Claude as the command agent (tool use in a plan, act, re-plan loop); the demo replays recorded real responses; the anthropic backend is written and not exercised (no key on the build machine).

rubric.Use of the data (30%): Record says who should be in each suite; twin gives rooms, routes and deletes impossible phone positions (two pucks become one point); aerial gives sides, approach and staging read by a vision tool; combined into 'phone B1, Suite 310, dentists, patients may be sedated, 17 m from Stair B'.
rubric.Agentic depth (30%): Situations as goals with a reply budget; the agent chooses tools (record, aerial vision, twin, phones, accountability) and ends in actions (assign with route, radio, EMS request, observations, record corrections); must search a ring or two candidates, never 'go to the phone'; re-called when geometry improves. Beacon turns use the labelled fallback policy until recorded.
rubric.Usefulness (25%): Incident commander and command post: who is inside, where, who is unaccounted for as an honest range, and a report at the end; prevention bureaus get a pre-plan draft for any commercial address.
rubric.Demo and polish (15%): One screen, two physical pucks and two iPhones, a printable report, a phone page for the rescue team that reads the feed; every uncertain thing drawn as uncertain.

limitations: No phone and no puck has been in the loop of any number reported; the live path (stock Qorvo firmware, lane L16's iOS app) is written, and the real range error of an iPhone against these boards is unmeasured

Opt-in only: a phone without the app is never ranged or identified; the most a puck could give is a Bluetooth device count, and devices are not people; the app must stay open with the screen on as built
Two pucks often leave two candidates; the twin removes one only when the geometry allows

All three sponsor layers are fixtures (real public data and NAIP imagery, synthetic interior); the live adapters were never called; the walls that prune a candidate are plausible walls, not surveyed ones
Expected head counts and life hazards are estimates and inferences from the record
Agent turns for the Beacon and Scout exercises fall back to a labelled deterministic policy until a real model run is recorded
Scout (radar) and Crews (tags) are simulation-only on these boards; the radar simulator was written alongside its detector
One floor modelled; feeds and the app link have no authentication; not a life-safety product

self_score_reasons.creativity: Using the building's own walls to decide between two possible phone positions is a new use of CoStar-style data; phones as a rescue sensor is not new in itself
self_score_reasons.utility: Runs end to end hands-free on the simulator with a real report and feeds; the live phone path has not been shown working yet
self_score_reasons.charity: Finding trapped and injured people sooner, with their own reported condition, is about as direct a public good as a hack can target
self_score_reasons.avidity: Three sensing modes, a reporting centre, a puck enclosure, a sourced feasibility answer and honest labels throughout
self_score_reasons.track_fit: Uses all three CoStar layers together and agentically, but only as fixtures; agent turns for the Beacon script are not yet recorded
self_score_reasons.demo_risk: The hands-free simulator run is safe; the live two-puck, two-iPhone demo depends on firmware, app and Wi-Fi working at the venue
